Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 92, verses 1–4:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Layl (The Night), because it opens with Allah's oath by the night when it covers the earth and what is upon it with its darkness.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• To draw attention to the diversity of creatures' deeds and the variety of their paths, and to explain the way of happiness and the way of misery, by mentioning some attributes of the righteous people of Paradise and some attributes of the wicked people of the Fire.

• To forbid people from being deceived by the wealth they have gathered, for it will not benefit them on the Day of Resurrection; to remind them of Allah's wisdom in clarifying for His servants the path of guidance and the path of misguidance; to warn of Allah's punishment for those who deny Allah's signs and His Messenger; and to set against this the depiction of a righteous believer who spends his wealth in good causes, so that he is saved from punishment and rewarded with the best reward.

[The Tafsir]

Allah, glorified is He, swears by the night when it covers the earth and what is upon it with its darkness, and by the day when it is revealed from the darkness of the night by its light, and by the creation of the pair: the male and the female. ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse.﴾ (Verse 4) Some work for this world and some work for the Hereafter.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, "the Simplified Tafsir") on surah 92, verses 17–21:

The one of utmost piety will be kept far away from it, the one who spends his wealth seeking more good. His spending is not a repayment to someone who had done him a favour, but he gives it seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High, and His pleasure. Allah will surely give him in Paradise what will please him.
